perspective:
From Vincent Chinana’s perspective, he has access to the following information:

- He is a mechanic and has a long-time friendship with Patrick Guzman, a construction worker. They have collaborated before, combining Vincent’s mechanical skills with Patrick’s construction expertise.
- At a diner, Vincent hears Patrick considering a new construction venture to expand Patrick’s business. Vincent tells Patrick he has heard it is risky and asks if Patrick is sure. Patrick says he thinks it is worth the risk but is still weighing options. Vincent warns that it could jeopardize financial security and suggests reconsidering or delaying until more information is gathered. Patrick says he appreciates the concern and will think it over.
- Over the next few days, Vincent notices Patrick avoiding detailed discussion about the investment.
- At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent says he feels Patrick is not telling him everything. Patrick says it is complicated and he did not want to worry Vincent with details. Vincent says that as a friend he feels betrayed by the lack of transparency. Patrick apologizes and agrees to sit down and explain everything.
- During a detailed discussion at Vincent’s garage, Vincent learns the investment situation is serious. Patrick tells him it has been tough and that he might lose a significant amount if it does not turn around soon. Vincent offers to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick thanks him and expresses gratitude for the support.
- A month later, Vincent learns or sees that the venture might actually turn a profit. At a coffee shop, Vincent says this to Patrick. Patrick says it is starting to look up and that he is relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologizes for doubting Patrick earlier and proposes a joint venture. Patrick agrees and suggests they work out the details.
- Later, at Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick are optimistic about the joint venture. Vincent says their combined skills can make it a success. Patrick agrees. Vincent says they should start drafting the business plan and outline every step carefully. Patrick agrees they should cover all bases and set it up for success.

Vincent does not have access to Patrick’s private thoughts, hidden events, narrator-only labels, or any information not stated to him or directly observed by him.
